This slice: EarClipNode.

```plato
//==
// # Triangulation
//
// The working record of the ear-clipping triangulator in
// `triangulation.library.plato`. Nothing else declares it and nothing else
// should read it: it is the node of a linked list held inside an affine
// `Buffer<EarClipNode>`, not part of the geometry vocabulary.

// One vertex of a ring being clipped. Prev and Next are BUFFER SLOTS, not pool
// indices — the two agree for an input vertex and differ for the duplicated
// vertices a hole bridge introduces, which is the whole reason the type carries
// Vertex separately. Active goes false when the vertex is clipped away or
// filtered out; its links are left intact so a walk standing on it can still
// step off.
//
// The node deliberately caches NO part of the ear test. Caching convexity and a
// blocker count per node is the obvious speed-up and it is unsound as usually
// written: clipping an ear can flip a neighbour from reflex to convex, which
// silently changes the blocker count of every OTHER candidate that vertex was
// blocking, not just of the two nodes the clip is local to. See the ear-clipping
// section of `triangulation.library.plato`.
type EarClipNode
{
    Vertex: VertexIndex;
    Prev: Integer;
    Next: Integer;
    Active: Boolean;
}
```
